changes: Repositories with >=2,000 stars fell from 59/80 to 8/80.
Repositories below 2,000 stars rose from 21/80 to 72/80.
Repositories created in 2025-2026 rose from 0/80 to 11/80.
Repositories pushed more than two years ago rose from 7/80 to 22/80.
The dominant-language pattern shifted from Python/C++ concentration to eight explicit language strata of 8 repositories each for Haskell, OCaml, Elixir, R, Swift, Zig, Lua, and Clojure.

remaining_biases: Wave 6 is intentionally stratified and therefore not representative of GitHub as a whole.
Low-star selection is concentrated mostly in the 500-1999 range; only 8/80 are below 500 stars.
Language balancing is artificial by design and should not be interpreted as ecosystem prevalence.
License metadata remains incomplete: 24/80 report UNKNOWN or NOASSERTION.
Very new repositories remain a minority even after correction.
Repository geography and organization type remain unmeasured.
next_requirements: Add a sub-500-star cohort larger than eight repositories.
Measure owner/org type and geography only when public metadata makes this meaningful and non-sensitive.
Expand exact license inspection for deep-inspected sources before implementation reuse.
Deep-inspect archived versus active implementations to separate historical lessons from current guidance.
Continue evidence-depth progression from README to source/tests/specifications rather than maximizing repository count.
